scopeChangeReason: Scope is the union of the five checklist items' declared file write-sets. The two create paths are the ported dossier client and the new smoke task. assets/ and both dist/ directories are gitignored build output regenerated by the allowed build commands, so they are excluded from the hand-edited surface rather than treated as source.

acknowledgements.reason: Not scope creep: this story's own in-scope change revoked a security pin, and re-approving it is work this story created and must close. That guard stores an exact content fingerprint of packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts on a dynamic-code-loading allowlist; its own comment states ANY edit to the handler revokes the approval until a human re-approves it. CHK-003 necessarily edited that handler to add --story, so the fingerprint moved and the guard failed, blocking REVIEW->TEST. Before re-pinning, the security question the pin exists to ask was answered: the DYNAMIC-CODE SURFACE IS UNCHANGED. A normalized diff of every await import(...), createRequire(...), eval( and new Function( occurrence in the handler against main reports no difference; the five approved loader call sites are byte-identical and only their line numbers shifted. The --story change adds string validation and URL construction only, introduces no new dynamic-code capability, and does not widen the --root-influenceable argument path this approval already accepts. The human re-approval the pin demands was obtained explicitly from the user before the fingerprint was touched, and the re-approval rationale is recorded in comments at both pin sites.

Not scope creep: this story's own CHK-005 work created the obligation, and leaving it unmet ships a repository whose entire root test suite aborts. CHK-005 added test:graph-story-flag-smoke to package.json's test:serial-reference, but RESOURCE_POLICY in full-suite-runner.ts is a THIRD membership authority beyond test:serial-reference and lattice.config.json's validate.commands. entriesFromSerialReference fails CLOSED on any serial-reference member lacking a policy entry, so the omission aborted the whole suite with 'canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[test:graph-story-flag-smoke]' rather than merely skipping the member; npm test exited 1 in 858ms, which is what blocked done_required_validate. The file's own comments record two prior stories (B-cdf6, B-49ed) hitting this identical trap and state the policy entry is mandatory, not optional. The entry added is the plain repoRead policy, which matches those precedents and is correct on the merits: the task only reads the repo and spawns the CLI against temporary directories, binds no port and holds no lock -- it asserts the opposite, that an unknown --story id is refused BEFORE any listener is created. Verified after the change: npm test now proceeds past inventory validation and executes the suite.

Not scope creep: this file is the canonical decision doc for the very command this story extends, it is named in CHK-005's relatedDocs, and two reviewer-filed findings required correcting it. F-002 (high, filed by the docs lane) found the 'Test-surface placement' section claimed only TWO test-membership authorities while RESOURCE_POLICY in full-suite-runner.ts is a third, fail-closed one; CHK-005 copied that two-list framing and consequently registered its new smoke task in two surfaces instead of three, which aborted the entire root test suite and blocked done_required_validate. F-004 (medium, same lane) then found the F-002 fix had corrected one occurrence but missed a SECOND stale claim in the same file, which also independently misstated that test:process-fact-contract is reached only through test:serial-reference when it carries repoRead('test:process-fact-contract') at full-suite-runner.ts:180. Leaving either uncorrected would ship a decision doc that actively causes the bug it exists to prevent, for the fourth time. Both fixes are documentation-only, verified claim-by-claim against code before committing, and independently re-verified by the concept, quality and docs lanes at the current tree. After the second fix the whole file and the entire live docs corpus (CLAUDE.md, README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/**) were swept for remaining stale two-surface framing; only two unrelated hits remain, and the docs and concept reviewers each re-ran that sweep independently rather than trusting the report.

Not scope creep: these are the framework's own dev-memory artifacts, written by the mandatory pre-DONE step. The DONE gate refuses the story with [missing_dev_memory_finish_decision] until dev_memory_finish_decision is recorded, and recording decision=captured requires the captured entries to exist first. Both files are therefore produced by running the gate's own required command, not by discretionary edits: experience.jsonl gained two lessons from this story (f40abd2, that registering a test task needs three fail-closed membership authorities rather than two, since omitting the RESOURCE_POLICY entry aborts the whole root suite; and 394c115, that signed artifacts auto-commit and re-stale one another so every mutation must be batched before the tree is frozen and verdicts earned), and finish-decisions/B-9f2c.json is the decision record itself. No product code or documentation is affected.

Acknowledged late, after the independent topology critic correctly caught that this file was edited across three repair rounds without ever being recorded in the scope contract, unlike the four other out-of-scope paths that were. That omission was mine and the critic was right to flag it as a real coverage gap. Why the edits were in scope for this story rather than creep: main commit 3aa57145d8 replaced the graph handler's refuse-before-listen path with ensureGraphClientBuilt, and this verifier still asserted the OLD contract, so npm --prefix packages/graph run check failed and blocked REVIEW to TEST. The story could not reach DONE without reconciling it. Three rounds followed because each repair was itself reviewed and found wanting: dcf54ecff3 adapted the contract but weakened coverage (F-005, caught by test-coverage with a negative control), 4912d8390a restored the content assertions but introduced a race and a process leak (F-006, caught by quality and reproduced live including an orphaned pid), and 0c9253c5be made the settle unconditional and polling-based (F-008, also caught by quality). Two residual limits remain recorded and deferred with evidence rather than chased: F-007 (deliberate padded-stub forgery, present-but-stale untestability) and F-009 (torn-write window; quality independently established production has no reachable trigger since its spawnSync carries no timeout). Every round was verified by re-running the check to exit 0 and by re-running the reviewers' own reproductions.
